name: Yevanic

ancestors.notes: Yevanic (Judeo-Greek) is a Greek dialect historically spoken by the Romaniote Jews, mutually intelligible with Greek and differing mainly in phonetic, intonational and lexical detail (Wikipedia: Yevanic).

Romaniotes wrote Greek and Yevanic texts in the Hebrew alphabet (attested from a 10th-century Hebrew-Greek glossary per Krivoruchko), and the language carries large amounts of Hebrew/Aramaic loan vocabulary; the switch to the Greek alphabet only came in the 19th century (Wikipedia: Yevanic; Jewish Languages Project: Judeo-Greek).

notes: Stub. Yevanic (Judeo-Greek, Romaniyka), the historic language of the Romaniote Jews of Greece, Anatolia and the Balkans, critically endangered (a few elderly speakers in Ioannina, Greece as of 2019; small groups documented in Iran as of 2021, per Wikipedia). Historically written in Hebrew square script with vowel points (nikkud) adapted to Greek phonology — attested from a 10th-century Hebrew-Greek glossary — before a 19th-century shift to the Greek alphabet for most surviving texts. No sourced letter-by-letter Hebrew-script grapheme-to-IPA correspondence table could be located this session (Omniglot's Yevanic page presents the alphabet only as unreadable chart images, not machine-readable text; Krivoruchko's philological work was not accessible for character-level detail). Grapheme inventory intentionally left empty rather than fabricated or borrowed wholesale from Modern Greek `el` graphemes, since the actual attested orthography is the Hebrew abjad, not the Greek alphabet. Wired to `el` as the base spoken variety and to `he` as the adstrate supplying both the historical script and the loan vocabulary.
